intro.title: Build replay attack defenses for signed requests
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Node.js server that defends against replay attacks on signed requests. You will learn to implement a nonce (a unique, one-time-use token) to ensure each signed request can only be processed once. The core programming concept involves using timestamps and in-memory storage to track and validate nonces. You will work with JavaScript, the Node.js built-in modules, and basic server-side logic. By the end, you will understand how to secure APIs by preventing attackers from reusing intercepted requests.
intro.usecase: Replay attack defenses are essential in payment processing APIs like Stripe or PayPal, where signed requests must be validated to prevent duplicate charges. E-commerce platforms implement these protections when handling webhook notifications for order confirmations or inventory updates. API gateways in microservices architectures use timestamp-based nonces to secure communication between internal services. Financial trading platforms and cryptocurrency exchanges rely on these mechanisms to ensure transaction requests can't be intercepted and replayed maliciously.
